problem:
Which of the following are logically equivalent to $Q?$

- $¬R∧(Q∧¬R)$
- $Q∧(¬R∨Q)$
- $(¬R∨Q)∧Q$
worked_solution:
The law that conjunction absorbs disjunction is stated as

$$
Q∧(Q∨¬R)≡Q.
$$

With that in mind, let's inspect each of the given statements.

- Statement I is *not* logically equivalent to $Q.$ This statement cannot be simplified using the absorption laws.

- Statement II is logically equivalent to $Q.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}Q∧(¬R∨Q) & ≡Q∧(Q∨¬R) \\  & ≡Q.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

- Statement III is logically equivalent to $Q.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}(¬R∨Q)∧Q & ≡Q∧(Q∨¬R) \\  & ≡Q.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."
